citations.evidenceText:
Newton – Euler Equation

Euler's equation
•   In a rigid body rotating with angular velocity 𝜔 and with
   angula acceleration ሶ𝜔, the moment 𝑁, which must be
   acting on the body to cause this motion, is given by
   Euler's equation
  ➢𝑁= 𝐶𝐼ሶ𝜔+ 𝜔× 𝐶𝐼𝜔,
•  where 𝐶𝐼 is the inertia tensor of the body written in a
   frame, {C}, whose origin is located at the center of mass.
•  𝐶𝐼𝜔 angular momentum of body.
•  Unlike F = ma, Euler's equation has an extra term ω × Iω
   that captures the gyroscopic effect — crucial for spinning
   robot joints and fast manipulation.


                                                                                                           9

solution.justification: I_Cω is angular momentum, and its inertial rate includes the transport term ω×I_Cω.

optionExplanations.o1: This is the source Euler equation.
optionExplanations.o2: This interchanges angular velocity and acceleration.
optionExplanations.o3: m v_C is linear momentum; the gyroscopic term need not vanish.
optionExplanations.o4: The cross term contributes to the moment, not the definition of H_C.

variables.I_C: inertia tensor about the center of mass in body-aligned axes

Inclusion of gravity forces in the dynamics algorithm

•  The effect of gravity loading on the links can be included quite simply by setting
